  lmao at “advice will be appropriated” my first question would be which brimstone ascent pro vod did you watch, but I see there’s a bigger issue to deal with for now my opinion is that its time to grind crosshair placement. Your crosshair is rarely in the correct spot at head height, even when you’re expecting an enemy. When you aren’t expecting an enemy, your crosshair is often in a wall or in the middle of nowhere, which isn’t even giving you a fighting chance when you get surprised. The exception is when you are peeking something with intent - your crosshair placement is much better, and I can tell you’ve been practicing this, but when we aren’t in that exact situation, our crosshair is everywhere. There’s only one way to fix this. I want you to focus ONLY on having your crosshair at head height and on an angle where enemies can come from for the next week. Basically, you’re going to try to have intent for the whole match. You will lose RR and ranked games as you stop focusing on the other aspects of your gameplay, but this is necessary to improve, and you must be willing to make this sacrifice. The only time your crosshair is allowed to not be at head height and on a dangerous angle is if your knife or utility is out.  After some time doing this, your crosshair placement will start to be good even when you aren’t focusing directly on it. Submit another VOD following these rules (your next ranked match) so I can make sure you’re doing them right, and then after one week submit a follow up VOD

- ## leo *—* 2024/10/26 16:34

  the major im noticing is that before you peek an angle, your crosshair is already in the wall- look at how you're pre-aiming angles. 4-5 steps before you even peek the angle, your crosshair is already prepared for that angle. Instead, you should be holding your crosshair a distance away from the wall first, then RIGHT BEFORE you peek the angle you're looking to peek, THEN you flick your crosshair into the wall to preaim. This should help you reduce the distance you need to move your crosshair when someone peeks you unexpectedly. Hope this helps! 

- ## Lolrus![身份组图标，UP S4: C10](https://cdn.discordapp.com/role-icons/1245120931182153748/efc17ac36a88f859f815fe0064478b14.webp?size=32&quality=lossless) *—* 2024/10/26 12:35

  1. crosshair placement is low in general, look at when you move around the map - it falls to the floor as you aim. some of this is mouse control (aim train if you arent already), but this should be something you are focusing on in, especially in dm. try playing a whole dm with your crosshair at head height for the most likely threat angle (eventually you should be doing this drill in ranked too at the cost of some RR but let's get that done in dm first)
  2. your movement is pretty weak in general, which is why you are getting insta killed so often. i see you slicing the pie which is good, but you sometimes do it in steps that are too small which is basically just causing you to peek slowly and so you get insta headshot. however, a bigger issue is your peeking with the W key which is also slowing your peeks and causing you to insta die. just focus on peeking with A and D for now. a popular dm drill is double binding your w key to your melee button. this means whenever you press w, you will pull out your knife, so the only way for you to take fights with your gun out is to peek with A and D. you'll have to run through corridors with w sometimes, and in those cases you will sprint through with your knife out, understanding that you are at risk of dying in these situations (you'll eventually learn that these areas where you are forced to hold W are areas you'll need to use utility to get through safely in comp)

  doing these should help you get into a lot more fights where you don't get one tapped, we can address other gunfighting skills easier afterwards since you'll be in gunfights longer TLDR: play dms focused on crosshair placement and peeking with A and D, double bind melee slot to your W key to help with this (woohoojin has talked about this drill b4 but i cant find the clip aaaa

- ## Kyomiro [류진], ![身份组图标，CM Sword](https://cdn.discordapp.com/role-icons/1070923891163279440/fd8d91f88c42e7041ad934c6c2784a00.webp?size=32&quality=lossless) *—* 2024/7/17 02:12

  Initial thoughts:

  - you can tell that you're trying to go for the head and not rush your shots which is a good thing
  - when you miss your first shot you often just keep trying to tap or will "micro step" and shoot again, this often led to you being killed because you're barely moving on the other person's screen
  - The fight on cypher at 4:03 was solid in that when he peeked you you moved away from his initial shot giving yourself time to aim
  - You seem to do well when the other person isn't moving or if they're moving but not looking at you (you'll correctly move your crosshair in front of their movement to intercept and click)
  - also in general, you're doing a solid job of trying to a/d to peek when anticipating a fight ![👍](https://discord.com/assets/a4faf6864a96a042.svg)

  Suggestions to improve:

  - Try this out first: go into a DM and when someone isn't facing you, you only get one bullet to kill, otherwise if you miss you let them kill you. BUT if they're facing you, you cannot shoot a bullet until they've shot first (should help you with moving to stay alive and giving you time to aim like in thatcypher fight)
  - After you feel comfortable with that: set up a replay buffer of about 4s in OBS, whenever you get a kill or die clip that 4s. Then at the end of the dm go over the kills/deaths (even if those deaths were dying from being shot in the back), identify why you won the fight or why you lost it or if you were uninentionally exposed to threats) and then queue another dm to work on those issues you identified

- ## frosty *—* 2024/6/26 13:38

  looking at the vod, first thing i noticed is your comms, no attempt was made to say "hi" to your teammates and to establish a relationship with them, and when you heard them coming A, you didn't take the time to tell your team that they were committing to A, or if you were unsure of that, you didn't comm how many people you saw on A. round 2: you need to play around your gun, you're saving and you have a classic, knowing that you have a classic on a save against their buy round, get ratty. play close angles that are annoying to go against so you can right click their ass. even if you don't kill them, you still get massive chip damage down, which helps your team kill them. on an eco round 2, your objective is not to win the round. it's super unlikely that you win the round, you want to deal as much damage as possible to their economy, so their round 3 bonus is as crappy as possible. how do you do this? make them waste util, play ratty angles, kill as many as possible. you don't exactly need to win the round, it would be great if you did. but damaging their eco is the main priority.  round 3: you're peeking off rip into B main with no utility to help you and without anyone to trade. a major mistake that's made in low elo is that players give out free 1v1s without being in a tradable position, if you die you're giving them a free rifle and nobody can get a trade off. peeking B main is okay, just get a teammate to play with you so if you die, theres at least an attempt at a trade  round 4: this is the kind of positioning that i'd wanna see if you peek B main, phoenix is prepared to peek out and trade you if they so happen ot be B main and kill you. fortunately there wasnt and they hit A, but i want to see you comming for a teammate to play with you when you peek of rip.

- ## jav [kdot], *—* 2024/6/13 19:31

  1. Mechanics

  Theres 2 main issues with your mechanics, your gamesense is weak so you dont know and can't anticipate where the enemy is coming from, when you peek or get peeked, your crosshair is never in the right spot to shoot the enemy. The second issue is you're really trigger happy and fire before your movement completely comes to a stop, I would reccomend woohoojin's overaim drill for iron-gold

  1. Gamesense

  Firstly, you should recognize they have been pushing mid every round and try to punish that more, call for teammates utility (Blind, Stuns, Vulnerable etc) Secondly, your teammates are really poorly coordinated despite actively using comms, your game plans in gold/plat should be kept simple I think you're overcooking it. (calling to fake with neon but all your teammates die before the fake is even executed?) (Faking A but your teammates push up mid and push A link?) Just keep things simple

  1. Utility

  You don't understand where smokes on site should go, for example you one way the box on C and die to an enemy holding backsite. Learn where smokes go on site (CT and Garage) watch pro vods to see where and when smokes are used. Seeing your tracker you're still really new to controller, so learn where to place smokes because it got you and your team killed

  1. Positioning

  Your positioning is really weak. you should recognize that the enemies have flashes and never stand out in the open unless you're HIM. You frequently find yourself in weak positions (exposed to multiple angles, out in the open when flashed etc) you can learn where controllers or, by looking at your tracker, you play sentinel mainly, watch how sentinel pros do it and copy them.) Nice Ace btw have a good one

  If you want to get better at aiming you should aimtrain. I know its kind of a touchy subject on this discord but since you asked my personal opinion I think aimtraining consistently is very helpful and will noticeably improve your aim. Most of aim is unconscious. When you go into a deathmatch with the goal to "aim in X way during this deathmatch" it's really hard because you can't try to properly apply and adjust a skill you haven't practiced a lot in real time. Find a playlist or routine or a few scenarios you like and play them every day for 20-30 mins. Try to pay attention to weaknesses (tracking, flicking, smoothness, etc.) and push your high scores. You will notice yourself becoming more confident with your reactions and hitting easy- to medium- difficulty shots much more effortlessly in deathmatch and in game, which will let you actually focus on other aspects like being "patient/calm" while aiming. My caveat is this: 50/50s are always going to be 50/50s. Gunfights will get easier as your aim becomes better and they will get hard again when you rank up and face more formidable players. At the end of the day, unless your aim is ESPECIALLY good or bad, when you swing a dry 1v1, you WILL lose about half of the time. It's not because you panic sprayed or didn't have fast enough reaction time or didn't have "patient/calm" aim, it's because you TOOK a 50/50 and the coin landed face down. If you want to get better at aiming, practice your aiming. If you want to get better at getting kills in valorant comp lobbies, practice taking ADVANTAGED fights that aren't 50/50s. Swing off a teammate. Jiggle peek and then swing wide. Ask for flash/recon. Lurk and shoot people in the back. Pay attention to your utility and your team's spacing and try to PUT yourself in FAVORABLE positions to make the kills EASIER for yourself. I promise this is the real secret to ranking up at the end of the day, even with mediocre aim.

- ## KittFoonya *—* 2024/6/10 08:43

  You have 2 problems that I see:

  1. Your entry pathing sucks, especially on B. Please watch one vod of TenZ or some other pro playing Jett on this map. I don’t even play Jett but I promise you TenZ is not throwing a smoke on the ground in B main and then dashing out of it into the open and hoping not to die. Watch where he smokes on B and where he dashes. Watch where he smokes on A and where he dashes. Copy it. Win. Easy.

  

  1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

  Hope this helps!

- ## KittFoonya *—* 2024/5/21 13:10

  On defense, you need to fight for space more proactively. Sitting backsite and waiting to see where the enemies push is almost always a bad idea unless you're playing cypher or killjoy. For smokes specifically (except viper), you almost always want to smoke somewhere at the start of the round and fight for it with 1-2 other teammates. On bind, smoke B long deep every round and fight it with one of your B players. If nobody is there, take the TP and crunch showers with one of your A players. If they come B, shoot them as they run through your smoke. For other maps, you can 1-way main or smoke mid (smoke tiles on ascent and double peek mid, smoke B main on sunset and fight it with a teammate, 1-way C on Lotus and have your jett or chamber go wide on mound, etc.). The key to this is that it gives you space and info, beyond just kill opportunities. If the enemies run through your smoke, you can kill them. If they don't, you have main smoked off so 1 person can hold it and you can play 3 people stacked on the other site. Primary takeaway: **You always want to have a PLAN for the round and ASK at least 1 teammate to DO something WITH you.** Hope this helps! 

- ## KittFoonya *—* 2024/5/21 13:10

  Hi. Your problem is that you play reactively instead of proactively. Your team is uncoordinated and you either win the round by killing 3 or watch your whole team die because you all went in without a plan. Your aim is good and your gunfight intuition is solid but you fail to put yourself in good positions and are forced to try and deal with whatever randomly happens in the round. Here's what to do instead: On attack, you need to be calling plays for your team. They can be simple (e.g. what you did on round 6 was good), but you almost never do this. It's not even about reading the enemy, it's about looking at what utility your team has and putting forward a barebones plan for how the round is going to go. "Gekko, flash our Raze into shower, she can take the space with her satchels. Reyna, come blind out short with me after I smoke." or "Cypher trip the shower push and sit A short, we're gonna make noise hookah and you can kill them if they try to TP." Honestly, from my perspective, it's a miracle you guys even won 5 rounds with no plan. Even in low immortal I've seen teams of 5 perfectly competent players run it down 5-man A short and lose because nobody called a shower split. You cannot play the game like this. Also, I see a lot of people do the smoke on A that cuts from dice to showers, and I don't understand why. I think this is a terrible smoke and you should almost never do this. If your team goes showers, you're cutting them off from helping you and making it so they can't peek anything by failing to smoke heaven or backsite. If nobody goes showers, (this is the WRONG way to play the map, but besides that,) you can't plant the bomb with no showers or backsite control. Even if you do, holding the post-plant is impossible if you only have short and maybe lamps unless the enemies magically forget that they have retake utility or they magically lose all of their gunfights. I would smoke both sides of dice to block off backsite and enable your team to hold space.

  Attack (Overtime):

  - The bomb is planted for long, hookah, and elbow. You have an Odin. You can spam from long. You need to double up with chamber and bait the shit out of your Clove, and if your Clove is smart, they would tuck backsite and wait for tap to peek bomb defuser off timing and then sit in tube and wait. It's a 3v2 on B. If you don't have elbow control then you need to give up site, ESPEICALLY if someone's coming from hookah.
  - The key to keeping B site is Elbow control. I need you to push up elbow once the bomb is down and get a kill. If you lose elbow then you need to fall back into hookah and/or long and play off tap/spam. Once you let people push out elbow and hookah you cannot hold B. It's why people take TP on retake in higher ranked lobbies, because you can take Hookah control and Elbow control and everyone on B site on Bind is pinched and will die.
  - In a fight against Odins, the key is to force the Odin to push you. All you have to do is hold an off angle against an Odin and simply head tap them once they swing into view because its a gun that's very immobile and cumbersome. Playing retake with the odin is very hard unless you're on ascent in which everything is fucking wallbangable.

  General:

  - scoped weapons are meant to hold angles, not to peek or push. When you're playing with an outlaw, marshal, or operator, you want to start at an aggressive angle and play a retreating battle. I want you to hold stuff, not peek stuff, and if you are going to peek I need you to slice the pie slowly. You have to be very patient if you're playing scoped weapons. I need you to hold at an off angle with a scoped weapon and STAY STILL.
  - 16:04 if you were just holding the off angle and didnt move (Clove wasnt even looking at you) you would've killed clove. Your shots are good but your movement with the operator/outlaw is bad. I need you to watch how Jett mains use the op.
  - don't be afraid to right click your knives or use a shorty in close range combat if you have an op.

  Defense:

  - after you get a kill don't overheat. I need you to get a kill and cloudburst yourself off at your feet (unless your multifrag potential is high, ie two enemies in front of you that arent looking at you). You often overheat and get yourself traded too quickly, you want to get a kill and fall back to keep numbers advantage and force the enemy team to make a play.
  - watch your omen at 12:32 to 12:45. That is how you should play defense. You may not need to tuck all the way into tree but you need to fall back and play off your teammate's utility or jiggle from cover.
